title: PM-Kisan's 24th Instalment of Rs 2,000 Reaches Farmers on October 30
excerpt: The October 30 payout to about 9.3 crore farmers depends on three portal checks — eKYC, Aadhaar bank seeding and land seeding — as a re-verification drive flags over 31 lakh cases.
body:
• The 24th PM-Kisan instalment of Rs 2,000 will be released on October 30, 2026, paid by direct benefit transfer into eligible farmers' bank accounts.
  • Whether the money arrives depends on three checks on the official portal: eKYC completed, Aadhaar seeded with the bank account, and land seeding marked "Yes" — any one marked "No" can hold the payment.
  • More than 31 lakh beneficiary cases have been flagged in a re-verification drive; farmers whose 23rd instalment was held only for a data or verification issue are expected to receive the pending Rs 2,000 together with this instalment once cleared.
  • Check your status today at pmkisan.gov.in under Farmers Corner > Know Your Status, or call the PM-Kisan helpline on 155261 or 1800-115-526.

The Centre will release the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-Kisan) scheme on October 30, 2026, transferring Rs 2,000 each to eligible farmer families across India, according to Mint and the scheme's official announcements. The date was confirmed on October 23 through the PM-Kisan portal and its official social media handle, which urged farmers to "mark your calendar" for the payout.

The instalment is expected to reach about 9.30 crore farmers, Karmactive reported, with the release event set in Banaskantha, Gujarat. The payment lands just before Diwali and during rabi sowing, when farm households face some of their highest expenses of the year.

Three checks decide whether the money lands

"The payment itself is scheduled for Thursday, October 30; farmers who find a "No" against any of the three indicators still have a short window to fix bank or eKYC records before the release."

PM-Kisan pays by direct benefit transfer, and the transfer only goes through if the beneficiary's records clear three verification indicators on the official PM-Kisan portal: land seeding, eKYC status, and Aadhaar bank seeding. If any indicator shows "No," the instalment may not be credited even if the farmer's name appears on the beneficiary list.

https://x.com/DRajput70111/status/2114331679636718064

eKYC can be completed through the PM-Kisan mobile app using face authentication, or at a Common Service Centre using biometrics. Aadhaar seeding and NPCI mapping problems have to be fixed at the farmer's bank. Farmers can check their village beneficiary list on the portal under Farmers Corner > Beneficiary List, and the scheme runs a helpline on 155261 and a toll-free line on 1800-115-526.

A re-verification drive has flagged over 31 lakh cases

This instalment follows a large re-verification exercise under updated eligibility rules. According to official data reported across national media, more than 31 lakh beneficiary cases have been flagged for physical verification. The flagged categories include households where both husband and wife were drawing the benefit — only one member of a family is eligible — accounts registered in the names of minors, and farmers who purchased their land after February 1, 2019, who are not eligible for the scheme.

Payments in flagged cases stay on hold until verification is completed. There is one relief for farmers caught by the drive: if the 23rd instalment was held back only because of a verification or data issue, the pending Rs 2,000 is expected to be released together with the 24th instalment once the record is cleared.

What the scheme pays, and what came before

Under PM-Kisan, eligible landholding farmer families receive Rs 6,000 a year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000, paid every four months. The previous, 23rd instalment was released on June 20, 2026, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi transferred more than Rs 18,880 crore to over 9.44 crore farmers from Tarakeswar in West Bengal, Rural Voice reported.

For diaspora families, the instalment matters in a practical way: many NRI households have parents or relatives farming family land in India, and the re-verification rules — one beneficiary per family, no post-2019 land purchases — are exactly the kind of record issue that surfaces when land has been partitioned or inherited. Families helping relatives check status from abroad can run the same portal check with the beneficiary's registration number. The payment itself is scheduled for Thursday, October 30; farmers who find a "No" against any of the three indicators still have a short window to fix bank or eKYC records before the release.

steps.detail: Go to pmkisan.gov.in and open the Farmers Corner section.
Enter your registration number and the captcha, then the OTP sent to your registered mobile.
Land Seeding, eKYC Done and Aadhaar Bank Seeding must all show Yes. Any No can hold the payment.
Complete eKYC on the PM-Kisan app or at a Common Service Centre; ask your bank to confirm Aadhaar seeding and NPCI mapping.
